title: Bounded algebraic coordinates give continuous split projections and finite overlap formulas
statement:
Let $K$ be a normed field [def-weil-field] and let $V$ be a normed $K$-vector space with an algebraic basis $(b_j)_{j\in J}$ and a chosen $j_0\in J$. Suppose $0<c\leq C<\infty$ and, for every finitely supported scalar family $(t_j)$,
$$c\max_j|t_j|\leq\Big\|\sum_jt_jb_j\Big\|\leq C\max_j|t_j|,$$
with empty maximum zero. Write $D=\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{cts}}_K(V)$, with composition as multiplication, and let $\lambda_j$ be the coordinate functions. Then $\lambda_j$ is continuous with $|\lambda_j(v)|\leq c^{-1}\|v\|$, and $E_{ij}(v)=\lambda_j(v)b_i$ belongs to $D$ with $\|E_{ij}(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$ and $E_{ij}E_{kl}=\delta_{jk}E_{il}$. Also $\theta_v(w)=\lambda_{j_0}(w)v$ belongs to $D$ and satisfies $\|\theta_v(w)\|\leq c^{-1}\|v\|\|w\|$. For every subset $A\subseteq J$, the coordinate projection $p_A(\sum_jt_jb_j)=\sum_{j\in A}t_jb_j$ belongs to $D$ with $\|p_A(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$. For $A,B\subseteq J$ one has $p_Ap_B=p_{A\cap B}$, and when $F=A\cap B$ is finite [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set],
$$p_Ap_B=\sum_{k\in F}E_{kk}=\sum_{k\in F}E_{k j_0}E_{j_0j_0}E_{j_0k}.$$
If $J=\mathbf N$ and $A\subseteq\mathbf N$ is infinite [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set], it has an increasing bijection $a_A:\mathbf N\to A$. The formulas $u_A(b_n)=b_{a_A(n)}$ and $r_A(b_{a_A(n)})=b_n$, with $r_A(b_m)=0$ for $m\notin A$, define elements of $D$ obeying
$$r_Au_A=1_D,\qquad u_Ar_A=p_A,\qquad p_Au_A=u_A,$$
and $\|u_A(v)\|,\|r_A(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$. All sums are finite algebraic expansions; completeness is not assumed.

proof.text: Write $v=\sum_jt_jb_j$ in its unique finite algebraic expansion and put $m(v)=\max_j|t_j|$, taking $m(0)=0$. Uniqueness gives $\lambda_j(v)=t_j$, $\lambda_j(v+w)=\lambda_j(v)+\lambda_j(w)$ and $\lambda_j(av)=a\lambda_j(v)$. The lower hypothesis gives $|\lambda_j(v)|\leq m(v)\leq c^{-1}\|v\|$. Applying the upper hypothesis to the family with coefficient $1$ at $i$ gives $\|b_i\|\leq C$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary, finite-coordinate norm estimates and split reindexings; the blueprint does not contain this auxiliary proof.

proof.text: The formulas $E_{ij}(v)=\lambda_j(v)b_i$ and $\theta_v(w)=\lambda_{j_0}(w)v$ are linear by step 1. Norm homogeneity gives $\|E_{ij}(v)\|=|\lambda_j(v)|\|b_i\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$ and $\|\theta_v(w)\|=|\lambda_{j_0}(w)|\|v\|\leq c^{-1}\|v\|\|w\|$. Apply [lem-sfb-additive-norm-bound-continuity] to each coordinate, matrix unit and fixed-$v$ map $\theta_v$, with constants $c^{-1}$, $C/c$ and $c^{-1}\|v\|$, respectively. The groups are normed additive groups, the maps additive, and these constants nonnegative. Hence the coordinates are continuous and these endomorphisms belong to $D$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary, finite-coordinate norm estimates and split reindexings; the blueprint does not contain this auxiliary proof.

proof.text: On a vector $w$, the coordinate of $b_k$ at $j$ is $\delta_{jk}$, so $E_{ij}E_{kl}(w)=\lambda_l(w)\lambda_j(b_k)b_i=\delta_{jk}E_{il}(w)$. Equality on all vectors is equality of endomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary, finite-coordinate norm estimates and split reindexings; the blueprint does not contain this auxiliary proof.

proof.text: For $A\subseteq J$ define $p_A(v)=\sum_{j\in A}t_jb_j$, summing only over the finite support of $v$. Uniqueness of coordinates shows this is linear, with coordinates $t_j$ on $A$ and zero elsewhere. Thus $m(p_A(v))\leq m(v)$ and $\|p_A(v)\|\leq C m(p_A(v))\leq(C/c)\|v\|$. The additive norm-bound criterion [lem-sfb-additive-norm-bound-continuity] applies, so $p_A\in D$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary, finite-coordinate norm estimates and split reindexings; the blueprint does not contain this auxiliary proof.

proof.text: The coefficient at $j$ of $p_Ap_B(v)$ is $t_j$ exactly when $j\in A\cap B$, and zero otherwise. This proves $p_Ap_B=p_{A\cap B}$. When $F=A\cap B$ is finite, $p_F(v)=\sum_{k\in F}\lambda_k(v)b_k=(\sum_{k\in F}E_{kk})(v)$. Step 3 gives $E_{k j_0}E_{j_0j_0}=E_{k j_0}$ and $E_{k j_0}E_{j_0k}=E_{kk}$, proving the second finite-sum identity. Empty $F$ gives the zero map.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary, finite-coordinate norm estimates and split reindexings; the blueprint does not contain this auxiliary proof.

proof.text: Now let $J=\mathbf N$ and $A\subseteq\mathbf N$ be infinite. Apply [lem-sfb-infinite-nat-increasing-enumeration] to obtain a strictly increasing bijection $a_A:\mathbf N\to A$. Define $u_A(\sum_nt_nb_n)=\sum_nt_nb_{a_A(n)}$ and $r_A(\sum_mt_mb_m)=\sum_{m\in A}t_mb_{a_A^{-1}(m)}$, again restricted to the input finite support. The bijection makes the output indices distinct, so both formulas are well-defined finite linear sums and are linear. They give exactly the prescribed values on every basis vector. By uniqueness of finite expansions, $r_Au_A(b_n)=b_n$, $u_Ar_A(b_m)=p_A(b_m)$, and $p_Au_A(b_n)=u_A(b_n)$; linearity extends all three identities to every vector.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent coefficient auxiliary, finite-coordinate norm estimates and split reindexings; the blueprint does not contain this auxiliary proof.

proof.text: Reindexing by the injection $a_A$ preserves the maximum of nonzero coefficient norms, so $m(u_A(v))=m(v)$. Deleting the coefficients outside $A$ and reindexing the rest gives $m(r_A(v))\leq m(v)$. Applying first the upper norm hypothesis to each output and then the lower norm hypothesis to the input gives $\|u_A(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$ and $\|r_A(v)\|\leq(C/c)\|v\|$. Apply [lem-sfb-additive-norm-bound-continuity] to these two additive maps to get $u_A,r_A\in D$. The identities in step 6 therefore hold in $D$, with $1_D$ the identity map. Every expansion used was finite, including when $J$ and $A$ are infinite.

lean.statement: theorem bounded_coordinate_split_projections (K : Type u) [NormedField K] (V : Type v) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace K V] (J : Type w) (b : Module.Basis J K V) (j₀ : J) (c C : ℝ) (_hc : 0 < c) (_hcC : c ≤ C) (_hb : ∀ t : J →₀ K, c * (↑(t.support.sup (fun j ↦ ‖t j‖₊)) : ℝ) ≤ ‖b.repr.symm t‖ ∧ ‖b.repr.symm t‖ ≤ C * (↑(t.support.sup (fun j ↦ ‖t j‖₊)) : ℝ)) : ∃ (lam : J → V →L[K] K) (E : J → J → V →L[K] V) (theta : V → V →L[K] V) (p : Set J → V →L[K] V), (∀ j : J, (lam j).toLinearMap = b.coord j) ∧ (∀ (j : J) (v₀ : V), ‖lam j v₀‖ ≤ c⁻¹ * ‖v₀‖) ∧ (∀ (i j : J) (v₀ : V), E i j v₀ = lam j v₀ • b i ∧ ‖E i j v₀‖ ≤ (C / c) * ‖v₀‖) ∧ (∀ i j k l : J, (j = k → E i j * E k l = E i l) ∧ (j ≠ k → E i j * E k l = 0)) ∧ (∀ v₀ w₀ : V, theta v₀ w₀ = lam j₀ w₀ • v₀ ∧ ‖theta v₀ w₀‖ ≤ c⁻¹ * ‖v₀‖ * ‖w₀‖) ∧ (∀ (A : Set J) (v₀ : V), p A v₀ = (b.repr v₀).sum (fun j t ↦ A.indicator (fun k ↦ t • b k) j) ∧ ‖p A v₀‖ ≤ (C / c) * ‖v₀‖) ∧ (∀ A B : Set J, p A * p B = p (A ∩ B)) ∧ (∀ (A B : Set J) (hF : (A ∩ B).Finite), p A * p B = ∑ k ∈ hF.toFinset, E k k ∧ p A * p B = ∑ k ∈ hF.toFinset, E k j₀ * E j₀ j₀ * E j₀ k)
